newsitem.title: UK: Aegon and AMP among favourites to buy Scot Am - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Aegon and AMP among favourites to buy Scot Am - S&P.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) are among the favourites to buy UK life insurance mutual Scottish Amicable, ratings agency Standard & Poor's told Reuters on Tuesday.

Martin Lees, S&P's specialist on the UK life insurance market, said AMP had already stated its interest in more UK acquisitions and that a company which uses independent financial advisors as its main means of distribution would be a good fit.
AMP, which is itself going through the demutualisation process, already owns UK life insurer Pearl but is said by industry sources to be less than satisfied with its performance.

Lees said he also liked the look of Aegon as a potential buyer. He said the Dutch group's previous acquisition of the UK's Scottish Equitable demonstrated its ability to provide extra capital to allow more aggressive development.
"I can't see any reason why Aegon couldn't run the two side by side as separate brands under one management, in the way that happens with Abbey Life and Scottish Mutual," said Rees.
"There is enough to distinguish the two," he added.
But Aegon declined to comment on the suggestion.
"We have no comment on this. It's just one of those market rumours," said Aegon spokesman Ewold de Bruijne in Amsterdam.
However, he added Aegon was interested in acquiring insurance companies in markets which it was familiar with.
"It's clear that Aegon has a strategy of acquiring companies in those countries where we already have an interest.
Aegon has an 80 percent stake in Scottish Equitable. It also has interests in the United States, Hungary and Spain as well as the Netherlands.
Speculation over the future of Scottish Amicable came after last week's offer of 1.4 billion pounds ($2.3 billion) from Abbey National.
Other companies which have since reported to be interested include ING, Prudential, Halifax, National Westminster, and Fortis.
Scottish Amicable plans to release details of its demutualisation and flotation plans at the beginning of next week. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
